title: A map of range
summary: Map the range over launch speed and angle at once: a straight 45° ridge in a vacuum, and a ridge that bends lower when air resistance joins in.

steps.title: Two inputs at once
steps.text:
A sweep varies one input. The Analyze ▸ Map tab varies two together and colours every result over the grid.

The setup maps launch speed from 10 to 60 m/s against launch angle from 25° to 60°: 90 throws, without air resistance. Press Run map and choose Range. The largest value is marked.

check.hint: Press Run map in the Analyze ▸ Map tab.
check.success: 367 m at 60 m/s and 45°: v₀²/g. The colours grow fast to the right because range goes as the square of the speed, but the best angle is 45° at every speed: a straight ridge.

steps.title: Now with air
steps.text:
Switch the model to "With drag" (a sphere of 5 cm radius and 1 kg) and run the same map again.

Drag grows with the square of the speed, so it matters little for a gentle lob and a lot for a fast throw. Follow the ridge from left to right: where is the best angle now?

checks.name: model
checks.hint: Set the Model to With drag.
Run the map again with drag on.

check.success: Only 232 m at best, against 367 m in a vacuum. At 10 to 30 m/s the ridge stays near 45°; at 40 m/s and above it slides down to about 42.5°.

steps.title: Which way does it bend?
steps.text: Compare the two maps. With drag, which way does the best launch angle move, and when?

options: Down, and more so the faster the throw
Up, and more so the faster the throw
It stays at 45°; only the range shrinks
check.hint: Look at where the ridge sits at 60 m/s.
check.success: Down. A high, slow arc spends a long time in the air for drag to work on; a flatter, faster throw loses less. The faster (or lighter) the ball, the stronger drag is against gravity, and the lower the best angle.
